questions.stem:
Truth-tellers & liars (3 speakers)

Alice says: “Charlie and Bob are both lying”
Bob says: “Charlie is telling the truth”
Charlie says: “Alice is lying or Bob is telling the truth”
Exactly 1 of these statements is false. Who is telling the truth and who is lying?
options: Alice is telling the truth; Bob is lying; Charlie is telling the truth
Alice is telling the truth; Bob is telling the truth; Charlie is lying

questions.stem:
Case-analysis puzzle (5 speakers) *

Amy says: “Dale is telling the truth only if Cara is telling the truth”
Ben says: “Eve is lying or Ben is telling the truth”
Cara says: “Dale is lying”
Dale * says: “exactly one of Dale and Cara is telling the truth”
Eve says: “at least one of Ben and Eve is telling the truth”
Constraint: at least 2 of the statements are false. (Speakers marked * are not bound to be truthful or lying — each may tell the truth or lie.) Which of the following must be true?
options: Amy must be telling the truth, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
Ben must be telling the truth, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
Cara must be telling the truth, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
Dale must be telling the truth, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
Amy must be lying, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
Eve must be telling the truth, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
Ben must be lying, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
Cara must be lying, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
questions.answer: Eve must be telling the truth, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
questions.solution:
Solution: With the constraint that at least 2 of the statements are false, and treating strict speakers as consistent and *-speakers as free, there are 3 consistent truth-assignments:Case 1: Amy=T, Ben=F, Cara=T, Dale=F, Eve=TCase 2: Amy=F, Ben=T, Cara=F, Dale=T, Eve=TCase 3: Amy=F, Ben=F, Cara=F, Dale=T, Eve=TAcross all of them, the only speaker whose status never changes is Eve, who is always truthful. Hence Eve must be telling the truth.
Why the distractors fail
A — Amy is lying in Cases 2 and 3, so she need not be truthful.
B — Ben is lying in Cases 1 and 3, so he need not be truthful.
C — Cara is lying in Cases 2 and 3, so she need not be truthful.
D — Dale is lying in Case 1, so he need not be truthful.
E — Amy is truthful in Case 1, so she need not be lying.
G — Ben is truthful in Case 2, so he need not be lying.
H — Cara is truthful in Case 1, so she need not be lying.

Case-analysis puzzle (5 speakers) *

Amy * says: “at least one of Eve and Dale is lying”
Ben says: “Cara is lying or Ben is telling the truth”
Cara says: “exactly one of Cara and Amy is telling the truth”
Dale * says: “at least one of Cara and Dale is telling the truth”
Eve * says: “exactly one of Cara and Amy is telling the truth”
Constraint: an even number of the statements are false. (Speakers marked * are not bound to be truthful or lying — each may tell the truth or lie.) Which of the following must be true?
options: Ben must be telling the truth, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
Dale must be lying, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
Cara must be telling the truth, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
Dale must be telling the truth, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
Amy must be lying, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
Eve must be telling the truth, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
Eve must be lying, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
Ben must be lying, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
questions.answer: Amy must be lying, regardless of which consistent case occurs.
questions.solution:
Solution: With the constraint that an even number of the statements are false, and treating strict speakers as consistent and *-speakers as free, there are 6 consistent truth-assignments. In every one of them Amy is lying. Hence Amy must be lying.
Why the distractors fail
A — Ben is lying in Cases 5 and 6, so he need not be truthful.
B — Dale is truthful in Cases 1, 3, and 5, so he need not be lying.
C — Cara is lying in Cases 3, 4, 5, and 6, so she need not be truthful.
D — Dale is lying in Cases 2, 4, and 6, so he need not be truthful.
F — Eve is lying in Cases 1, 4, and 6, so she need not be truthful.
G — Eve is truthful in Cases 2, 3, and 5, so she need not be lying.
H — Ben is truthful in Cases 1–4, so he need not be lying.
